218	type ComputedTemplates = {
219	  contexts: CategoryTemplateContext[];
220	  errors: string[];
221	  orphanGoals: TemplateGoal[];
222	};
223	
224	async function computeTemplates(
225	  month: string,
226	  force: boolean,
227	  categoryTemplates: Record<CategoryEntity['id'], Template[]>,
228	  categories: CategoryEntity[] = [],
229	  skipAvailableClamp: boolean = false,
230	): Promise<ComputedTemplates> {
231	  // setup categories
232	  const isTracking = isTrackingBudget();
233	  if (!categories.length) {
234	    categories = (await getCategories()).filter(
235	      c => isTracking || !c.is_income,
236	    );
237	  }
238	
239	  // setup categories to process
240	  const templateContexts: CategoryTemplateContext[] = [];
241	  let availBudget = await getSheetValue(
242	    monthUtils.sheetForMonth(month),
243	    `to-budget`,
244	  );
245	  const prioritiesSet = new Set<number>();
246	  const errors: string[] = [];
247	  const orphanGoals: TemplateGoal[] = [];
248	  for (const category of categories) {
249	    const { id } = category;
250	    const sheetName = monthUtils.sheetForMonth(month);
251	    const templates = categoryTemplates[id];
252	    const budgeted = await getSheetValue(sheetName, `budget-${id}`);
253	    const existingGoal = await getSheetValue(sheetName, `goal-${id}`);
254	
255	    // only run categories that are unbudgeted or if we are forcing it
256	    if ((budgeted === 0 || force) && templates) {
257	      try {
258	        const templateContext = await CategoryTemplateContext.init(
259	          templates,
260	          category,
261	          month,
262	          budgeted,
263	          skipAvailableClamp,
264	        );
265	        // don't use the funds that are not from templates
266	        if (!templateContext.isGoalOnly()) {
267	          availBudget += budgeted;
268	        }
269	        availBudget += templateContext.getLimitExcess();
270	        templateContext.getPriorities().forEach(p => prioritiesSet.add(p));
271	        templateContexts.push(templateContext);
272	      } catch (e) {
273	        errors.push(`${category.name}: ${e.message}`);
274	      }
275	
276	      // do a reset of the goals that are orphaned
277	    } else if (existingGoal !== null && !templates) {
278	      orphanGoals.push({
279	        category: id,
280	        goal: null,
281	        longGoal: null,
282	      });
283	    }
284	  }
285	
286	  if (errors.length > 0) {
287	    return { contexts: templateContexts, errors, orphanGoals };
288	  }
289	
290	  const priorities = new Int32Array([...prioritiesSet]).sort((a, b) => a - b);
291	  // run each priority level
292	  for (const priority of priorities) {
293	    const availStart = availBudget;
294	    for (const templateContext of templateContexts) {
295	      const budget = await templateContext.runTemplatesForPriority(
296	        priority,
297	        availBudget,
298	        availStart,
299	      );
300	      availBudget -= budget;
301	    }
302	  }
303	
304	  distributeRemainder(templateContexts, availBudget);
305	
306	  return { contexts: templateContexts, errors, orphanGoals };
307	}
308	
309	async function processTemplate(
310	  month: string,
311	  force: boolean,
312	  categoryTemplates: Record<CategoryEntity['id'], Template[]>,
313	  categories: CategoryEntity[] = [],
314	): Promise<Notification> {
315	  const { contexts, errors, orphanGoals } = await computeTemplates(
316	    month,
317	    force,
318	    categoryTemplates,
319	    categories,
320	  );
321	
322	  if (contexts.length === 0 && errors.length === 0) {
323	    if (orphanGoals.length > 0) {
324	      await setGoals(month, orphanGoals);
325	    }
326	    return {
327	      type: 'message',
328	      message: 'Everything is up to date',
329	    };
330	  }
331	  if (errors.length > 0) {
332	    return {
333	      sticky: true,
334	      message: 'There were errors interpreting some templates:',
335	      pre: errors.join(`\n\n`),
336	    };
337	  }
338	
339	  const budgetList: TemplateBudget[] = [];
340	  const goalList: TemplateGoal[] = [...orphanGoals];
341	  contexts.forEach(context => {
342	    const values = context.getValues();
343	    budgetList.push({
344	      category: context.category.id,
345	      budgeted: values.budgeted,
346	    });
347	    goalList.push({
348	      category: context.category.id,
349	      goal: values.goal,
350	      longGoal: values.longGoal ? 1 : null,
351	    });
352	  });
353	  await setBudgets(month, budgetList);
354	  await setGoals(month, goalList);
355	
356	  return {
357	    type: 'message',
358	    message: `Successfully applied templates to ${contexts.length} categories`,
359	  };
360	}
361	
362	export type DryRunCategoryResult = {
363	  budgeted: number;
364	  perTemplate: number[];
365	};
366	
367	export async function dryRunCategoryTemplate({
368	  month,
369	  categoryId,
370	  templates,
371	}: {
372	  month: string;
373	  categoryId: CategoryEntity['id'];
374	  templates: Template[];
375	}): Promise<DryRunCategoryResult> {
376	  // The projection answers "how much do these templates demand" — it
377	  // skips the priority clamp so future months (where To Budget is empty)
378	  // still show the templates' intended amount instead of 0.
379	  const { data: categoryData }: { data: CategoryEntity[] } = await aqlQuery(
380	    q('categories').filter({ id: categoryId }).select('*'),
381	  );
382	  if (categoryData.length === 0) {
383	    return { budgeted: 0, perTemplate: templates.map(() => 0) };
384	  }
385	  const { contexts } = await computeTemplates(
386	    month,
387	    true,
388	    { [categoryId]: templates },
389	    categoryData,
390	    true,
391	  );
392	  const ctx = contexts.find(c => c.category.id === categoryId);
393	  if (!ctx) return { budgeted: 0, perTemplate: templates.map(() => 0) };
394	  const values = ctx.getValues();
395	  return {
396	    budgeted: values.budgeted,
397	    perTemplate: templates.map(t => values.perTemplateContribution.get(t) ?? 0),
398	  };
399	}

import type { CategoryEntity } from '#types/models';

export type CategoryWithSubcategories<T extends CategoryEntity> = T & {
  subcategories: T[];
};

/**
 * Turns a group's flat category list into top-level categories, each with
 * its subcategories. Order is kept within each level. A subcategory whose
 * parent isn't in the list (hidden, deleted or in another group) is
 * treated as a top-level category so it never disappears.
 */
export function nestCategories<T extends CategoryEntity>(
  categories: T[],
): CategoryWithSubcategories<T>[] {
  const ids = new Set(categories.map(cat => cat.id));
  const subcategoriesByParent = new Map<CategoryEntity['id'], T[]>();
  const topLevel: T[] = [];

  for (const cat of categories) {
    if (cat.parent_id && ids.has(cat.parent_id)) {
      const siblings = subcategoriesByParent.get(cat.parent_id) ?? [];
      siblings.push(cat);
      subcategoriesByParent.set(cat.parent_id, siblings);
    } else {
      topLevel.push(cat);
    }
  }

  return topLevel.map(cat => ({
    ...cat,
    subcategories: subcategoriesByParent.get(cat.id) ?? [],
  }));
}

/** Whether a category is a subcategory of another category. */
export function isSubcategory(category: Pick<CategoryEntity, 'parent_id'>) {
  return category.parent_id != null;
}

```typescript
import type { CategoryEntity } from '#types/models';

import { isSubcategory, nestCategories } from './categories';

function category(
  id: string,
  parent_id: string | null = null,
): CategoryEntity {
  return { id, name: id, group: 'group1', parent_id };
}

function shape(categories: CategoryEntity[]) {
  return nestCategories(categories).map(cat => [
    cat.id,
    cat.subcategories.map(sub => sub.id),
  ]);
}

describe('nestCategories', () => {
  it('puts subcategories under their parent and keeps the order', () => {
    expect(
      shape([
        category('rent'),
        category('food'),
        category('groceries', 'food'),
        category('restaurants', 'food'),
        category('fun'),
      ]),
    ).toEqual([
      ['rent', []],
      ['food', ['groceries', 'restaurants']],
      ['fun', []],
    ]);
  });

  it('nests a subcategory listed before its parent', () => {
    expect(shape([category('restaurants', 'food'), category('food')])).toEqual(
      [['food', ['restaurants']]],
    );
  });

  it('shows a subcategory whose parent is missing as top-level', () => {
    expect(shape([category('restaurants', 'deleted')])).toEqual([
      ['restaurants', []],
    ]);
  });

  it('never hides a category nested two levels deep', () => {
    expect(
      shape([category('z'), category('y', 'z'), category('x', 'y')]),
    ).toEqual([
      ['z', ['y']],
      ['x', []],
    ]);
  });

  it('never hides categories that are each other’s parent', () => {
    expect(shape([category('a', 'b'), category('b', 'a')])).toEqual([
      ['a', []],
      ['b', []],
    ]);
  });
});

describe('isSubcategory', () => {
  it('is true only when the category has a parent', () => {
    expect(isSubcategory(category('restaurants', 'food'))).toBe(true);
    expect(isSubcategory(category('food'))).toBe(false);
    expect(isSubcategory({})).toBe(false);
  });
});

```

_**Agent (claude-opus-5-5 2026-10-01 17:23:13Z)**_

Steps 3b and 4 are done. All tests pass, `yarn typecheck` passes, and lint is clean. That's the 227 budget and API tests after 3b, then 87 loot-core tests and 6 client mutation tests after step 4.

## Step 3b: your three decisions, on the server

**1. A subcategory is capped at its parent's budget.** In `setCategoryBudget`, an increase is limited to what the parent has budgeted that month, with a negative parent counting as $0. Decreases always work and give the money back.
- Food has $100 and you ask for $150 on Restaurants: Restaurants gets $100 and Food goes to $0.
- If Food has nothing, the subcategory stays at $0.

The same cap applies to copy last month for one category, a single category's average, and copy until year end.

**2. "To Budget" can't fund a subcategory.** The server now throws "A subcategory can only be funded from its parent category, not To Budget" in three actions:
- `transferAvailable`, the "To Budget" move-to-category option;
- `coverOverspending`, when covering from "To Budget";
- `transferCategory`, when moving from "To Budget".

The check runs before any write, so a rejected request changes nothing. Covering or transferring from a named category, including the parent, still works. Those three actions are back to plain writes, because after the check the only money source left is a named category.

**3. Templates skip subcategories.** I changed three places:
- **`getTemplates`** ignores subcategories. Every apply path reads from it, so applying templates, overwriting, applying a selection, applying one category and the automations view all skip them.
- **The template preview** (`dryRunCategoryTemplate`) gets its templates passed in, so it needed its own check. It shows $0 for a subcategory, so the preview doesn't promise money that will never come.
- **End-of-month cleanup** leaves subcategories out of the categories it reads.

**Tests:** 8 new ones cover the cap, its limit cases, each of the three blocked actions, a parent covering its subcategory, and templates. In the template test, Food's template budgets $100 and the identical one on Restaurants budgets nothing. I also updated two step 3 tests that expected the old behavior.

## Step 4: client data

**Shared tree helper:** a new [shared/categories.ts](packages/loot-core/src/shared/categories.ts) has:
- **`nestCategories`**, which turns a group's flat list into parents, each with its `subcategories`;
- **`isSubcategory`**, which says whether a category has a parent.

The server's ordering from step 2 now uses `nestCategories` too, so the server's flat list order and the budget page's tree can't disagree. While writing it I found that a category nested two levels deep, which conflicting edits on two devices could produce, would have disappeared. The helper now shows those as top-level, and the tests cover chains, loops and a missing parent.

**Mutations:** in [mutations.ts](packages/desktop-client/src/budget/mutations.ts), `useCreateCategoryMutation` takes an optional `parentId`, and `useSaveCategoryMutation` passes a new category's `parent_id` through. Nesting and un-nesting an existing category already works through `useUpdateCategoryMutation`, thanks to the `null` fix in step 3. Two new tests cover creating a subcategory through each path.

## Step 5 needs to

- **New row:** set `parent_id` on the placeholder category it builds.
- **Hidden parents:** nest a group's categories before filtering out hidden ones, so a hidden parent's subcategories are hidden with it rather than showing up as top-level rows.
- **Hide the blocked options on subcategory rows:** the "To Budget" picker target, cover from "To Budget", and the template and automation options. The server rejects these now, but the menus still offer them.

Step 5, the budget page UI, is next.

<tool-use data-tool-type="generic" data-tool-name="AskUserQuestion"><details>
<summary>Tool use: **AskUserQuestion**</summary>
**What should a parent category's Budgeted cell show?**

Options:
- **Own share + total hint (Recommended)** - The Budgeted cell keeps showing and editing the parent's own share, the part not given to subcategories, so Budgeted − Spent = Balance stays true on every row. A small 'Total: $X' line or tooltip shows the parent plus its subcategories.
- **Total in the cell** - The Budgeted cell shows and edits the parent total; editing it sets own share = total − subcategories, capped at zero. Budgeted − Spent no longer equals Balance on parent rows.

**Should existing categories be nestable, or only new ones created as subcategories?**

Options:
- **Also nest existing (Recommended)** - Add a 'Make subcategory of…' menu item with a picker limited to valid parents in the same group. The server already supports it. This is more UI, but users don't have to recreate categories.
- **New subcategories only** - Only 'Add subcategory' and 'Remove from parent'. Smaller step 5. Existing categories can't be moved under a parent from the UI.

**Should a parent's subcategories be collapsible on the budget page?**

Options:
- **No, always shown (Recommended)** - Subcategories always show under their parent; collapsing the group still hides everything. Keeps step 5 smaller.
- **Yes, add a toggle** - A chevron on parent rows that collapses its subcategories, saved like group collapse. More UI and keyboard-navigation work.


**Answer:** Own share + total hint (Recommended), Also nest existing (Recommended), No, always shown (Recommended)
</details></tool-use>

1	import { useCallback, useRef } from 'react';
2	import type { RefObject } from 'react';
3	
4	import type { Falsy } from '@actual-app/core/types/util';
5	
6	import {
7	  addItems,
8	  setContextMenuPosition,
9	} from '#contextmenu/contextMenuSlice';
10	import type { ContextMenuItem } from '#contextmenu/types';
11	import { useRefEventListener } from '#hooks/useRefEventListener';
12	import { useDispatch } from '#redux';
13	
14	type UseContextMenuProps = {
15	  triggerRef: RefObject<HTMLElement | null>;
16	  enabled?: boolean;
17	  items: Falsy<ContextMenuItem>[];
18	};
19	
20	export function useContextMenu({
21	  triggerRef,
22	  enabled = true,
23	  items,
24	}: UseContextMenuProps) {
25	  const dispatch = useDispatch();
26	
27	  // Store actions in a ref to avoid re-binding the event listener on every render
28	  const actionsRef = useRef(items);
29	  actionsRef.current = items;
30	
31	  const processedItems = items.filter(
32	    item => item && (typeof item === 'symbol' || !item.hidden),
33	  ) as ContextMenuItem[];
34	
35	  useRefEventListener(triggerRef, 'contextmenu', (e: MouseEvent) => {
36	    if (enabled) {
37	      e.preventDefault();
38	      dispatch(addItems(processedItems));
39	      dispatch(setContextMenuPosition({ x: e.clientX, y: e.clientY }));
40	    }
41	  });
42	
43	  const handleContextMenu = useCallback(() => {
44	    if (!triggerRef.current || !enabled) return;
45	    const rect = triggerRef.current.getBoundingClientRect();
46	    // prefer MouseEvent bubbling over dispatching events to
47	    // allow nesting context menu actions
48	    triggerRef.current.dispatchEvent(
49	      new MouseEvent('contextmenu', {
50	        clientX: rect.x,
51	        clientY: rect.y + rect.height,
52	        bubbles: true,
53	      }),
54	    );
55	  }, [triggerRef, enabled]);
56	
57	  return { handleContextMenu };
58	}
59

import { Trans, useTranslation } from 'react-i18next';

import { Text } from '@actual-app/components/text';
import { theme } from '@actual-app/components/theme';
import { Tooltip } from '@actual-app/components/tooltip';
import { View } from '@actual-app/components/view';
import type { TransObjectLiteral } from '@actual-app/core/types/util';

import { FinancialText } from '#components/FinancialText';
import { useFormat } from '#hooks/useFormat';

type ParentTotalHintProps = {
  /** The category's own budget, the part not given to subcategories. */
  budgeted: number;
  /** Own budget plus everything its subcategories hold. */
  total: number;
};

// Shown next to a parent category's budget when its subcategories hold
// money, so the parent's full amount is still visible. Categories without
// subcategories always have total === budgeted, so they show nothing.
export function ParentTotalHint({ budgeted, total }: ParentTotalHintProps) {
  const { t } = useTranslation();
  const format = useFormat();

  if (total === budgeted) {
    return null;
  }

  const amount = format(total, 'financial');

  return (
    <Tooltip
      content={
        <Trans>
          Total with subcategories:{' '}
          <FinancialText>{{ amount } as TransObjectLiteral}</FinancialText>
        </Trans>
      }
      placement="bottom"
    >
      <View
        aria-label={t('Total with subcategories: {{amount}}', { amount })}
        data-testid="parent-total-hint"
        style={{
          justifyContent: 'center',
          paddingLeft: 3,
          borderTopWidth: 1,
          borderBottomWidth: 1,
          borderColor: theme.tableBorder,
        }}
      >
        <Text style={{ color: theme.pageTextLight, fontSize: 11 }}>Σ</Text>
      </View>
    </Tooltip>
  );
}

Step 5 is implemented, but I haven't seen it running in the app yet. Typecheck passes, lint shows nothing new, and the client unit tests pass (185, including 15 new ones for the helpers). The running-app check is in step 6.

`yarn generate:i18n` rewrote `packages/desktop-client/locale/en.json`, but that file isn't in `git status`, so it looks like a generated file that isn't committed. I didn't check whether it's ignored.

**Rows and sidebar:**
- **Subcategories show under their parent, indented.** Rows are built by a new `getCategoryRows` in [util.ts](packages/desktop-client/src/components/budget/util.ts), which nests before filtering hidden categories, so a hidden parent hides its subcategories too.
- **Category menu** ([SidebarCategory.tsx](packages/desktop-client/src/components/budget/SidebarCategory.tsx)):
  - "Add subcategory" opens an indented "New subcategory name" row under the parent.
  - "Make subcategory of…" opens a picker listing other top-level categories in the same group. It isn't offered on categories that already have subcategories.
  - "Remove from parent" appears on subcategories.

**Parent total:** when a parent's subcategories hold money, a small **Σ** appears next to the parent's budget number. Hovering shows "Total with subcategories: $X", and the same text is the marker's accessible label. Otherwise nothing extra shows. This is the new [ParentTotalHint.tsx](packages/desktop-client/src/components/budget/ParentTotalHint.tsx), used by both the envelope and tracking budgets.

**What's hidden on subcategories:**
- "Overwrite with template" in the budget menu, for both budget types.
- The automations button in the sidebar.
- In the "To Budget" picker for moving money, subcategories aren't listed.
- When covering a subcategory's overspending, "To Budget" isn't offered as a source. Its parent and other categories still are.

**Drag-and-drop** ([BudgetTable.tsx](packages/desktop-client/src/components/budget/BudgetTable.tsx), via the new `getCategoryDropTarget`):
- A subcategory only moves among its siblings; other drops do nothing.
- A top-level category dropped onto a subcategory row lands after that parent's block.

**Deleting** a subcategory with transactions preselects its parent as the transfer target, and you can still pick another category.

**Things to look at in the app:**
- **The Σ marker:** it's my own choice for the "total hint", so it might look out of place.
- **Indent:** subcategory rows are indented 16px, and I haven't seen how that looks.
- **The picker popover:** it's anchored to the category name.

Step 6 is next: the release note, the Playwright end-to-end test, the full `yarn test` and `yarn lint:fix` runs, and running the app with the demo budget to check this UI. I'll report any visual-regression snapshots that change rather than updating them silently.

# Writing Release Notes for actualbudget/actual

Release notes are the user-facing changelog. Each code change adds one Markdown file to `upcoming-release-notes/`, and these get collected into the published changelog at the next release. The authoritative source is the **Writing Good Release Notes** section of `packages/docs/docs/contributing/index.md`. Read it if anything below is unclear.

## The file

Create `upcoming-release-notes/<slug>.md`, where `<slug>` is a **short, descriptive kebab-case slug** naming the change (e.g. `add-payee-autocomplete.md`, `fix-mobile-category-delete.md`). Do **not** use a PR number, since the PR link is resolved automatically at release time. (Numeric filenames like `1234.md` still work, but a slug is preferred.)

```markdown
---
category: Features
authors: [YourGitHubUsername]
---

Add payee autocomplete to the transaction entry form
```

- **`category`**: exactly one of `Features` (new feature), `Enhancements` (improvement to an existing feature), `Bugfix` (bug fix), or `Maintenance` (internal change with no user-visible effect).
- **`authors`**: array of the GitHub username(s) who did the work.

## Writing the entry

The body is the changelog line. It is read by everyday users, not developers.

- **One sentence.** Short and clear. No paragraphs, no bullet lists, no long prose.
- **Plain language, no technical detail.** Describe what changed for the user, not how it was built. Avoid file names, function names, internal component names, and implementation jargon. (Exception: `Maintenance` entries may be technical, since they are for internal changes.)
- **Phrase it as a command.** Start with a present-tense verb: "Add …", "Fix …", "Show …", not "Added …" or "Adds …".
- Generally match the PR title, but reword it if that reads more clearly to a user.

Good: `Fix incorrect balance when reconciling an account with future transactions`
Too technical: `Fix off-by-one in reconcileTransactions() when txn.date > today`

cd "C:/Users/icsab/actual-budget/actual-budget" && cat >> packages/desktop-client/e2e/budget.test.ts <<'EOF'

test.describe('Budget subcategories', () => {
  let page: Page;
  let configurationPage: ConfigurationPage;
  let budgetPage: BudgetPage;

  test.beforeEach(async ({ browser }) => {
    page = await browser.newPage();
    configurationPage = new ConfigurationPage(page);

    await page.goto('/');
    budgetPage = await configurationPage.createTestFile();
    await page.mouse.move(0, 0);

    // Start from a known parent amount; the demo's amounts vary by month
    await budgetPage.setBudgetedAmount('Food', '200');
    await expect
      .poll(() => budgetPage.getBudgetedForCategory('Food'))
      .toBe(20000);
    await budgetPage.addSubcategory('Food', 'Dining Out');
  });

  test.afterEach(async () => {
    await page?.close();
  });

  test('a subcategory is listed under its parent and funded from it', async () => {
    const names = await budgetPage.getCategoryNames();
    expect(names[names.indexOf('Food') + 1]).toBe('Dining Out');

    const totalBefore = await budgetPage.getTotalBudgetedAmount();
    await budgetPage.setBudgetedAmount('Dining Out', '50');

    await expect
      .poll(() => budgetPage.getBudgetedForCategory('Dining Out'))
      .toBe(5000);
    await expect
      .poll(() => budgetPage.getBudgetedForCategory('Food'))
      .toBe(15000);
    expect(await budgetPage.getTotalBudgetedAmount()).toBe(totalBefore);
    await expect(
      budgetPage
        .getCategoryRow('Food')
        .getByTestId('parent-total-hint')
        .first(),
    ).toBeVisible();
  });

  test('a subcategory cannot take more than its parent has', async () => {
    await budgetPage.setBudgetedAmount('Food', '100');
    await expect
      .poll(() => budgetPage.getBudgetedForCategory('Food'))
      .toBe(10000);

    await budgetPage.setBudgetedAmount('Dining Out', '250');

    await expect
      .poll(() => budgetPage.getBudgetedForCategory('Dining Out'))
      .toBe(10000);
    await expect
      .poll(() => budgetPage.getBudgetedForCategory('Food'))
      .toBe(0);
  });

  test('removing a subcategory from its parent keeps its money', async () => {
    await budgetPage.setBudgetedAmount('Dining Out', '50');
    await expect
      .poll(() => budgetPage.getBudgetedForCategory('Food'))
      .toBe(15000);

    await budgetPage.removeFromParent('Dining Out');

    await expect(
      budgetPage.getCategoryRow('Food').getByTestId('parent-total-hint'),
    ).toHaveCount(0);
    expect(await budgetPage.getBudgetedForCategory('Dining Out')).toBe(5000);
    expect(await budgetPage.getBudgetedForCategory('Food')).toBe(15000);
  });
});
EOF

Step 6 is done, and the feature works in a real browser: all three subcategory end-to-end tests pass, and a screenshot walkthrough in Edge looked right. Nothing is committed yet.

**How I ran the browser tests without installing anything:** the Playwright browser download stalled, so I pointed Playwright at the Microsoft Edge already on your machine. That used a temporary config in the scratchpad, so nothing in the repo changed. I also started the dev server myself and ran the tests one at a time, because the first attempts timed out before the app even loaded.

**Results:**
- **End-to-end tests:** all 3 of mine pass. Of the 8 existing tests in `budget.test.ts`, 7 pass. The eighth, "right clicking budget name opens context menu", timed out before the app loaded. My first subcategory test hit the same timeout in the full run, then passed in 18 seconds when rerun alone, so I believe the existing test failed for the same reason. I didn't rerun it.
- **Unit tests and typecheck:** pass, except the known `main.test.ts` `EEXIST` failure, which I've left alone as you asked. `yarn generate:i18n` creates a gitignored `locale/` folder that breaks the client mutation tests, so I moved it to the scratchpad. Anyone who runs that command locally will see the same failures.
- **Lint:** clean on my files. `yarn lint:fix` also reformatted about 465 files I hadn't touched, including teammates' AI logs. I restored all of them; none had uncommitted work.
- **Release note:** [add-budget-subcategories.md](upcoming-release-notes/add-budget-subcategories.md), credited to `icsasso` under Features.

**What the screenshots showed:**
- Subcategories sit indented under their parent.
- Budgeting 50.00 and 30.00 to two subcategories lowered Food from 200.00 to 120.00. "To Budget" stayed at 200.00, and the totals didn't move.
- The Σ tooltip on Food reads "Total with subcategories: 200.00".
- Food's menu offers "Add subcategory" but not "Make subcategory of…", since it already has subcategories. A subcategory's menu offers "Remove from parent" instead.
- The "Move under" picker lists only top-level categories in the same group. Moving Restaurants under Food indented it, kept its 300.00, and left the totals unchanged.

**Not checked:**
- **Visual regression snapshots:** Docker isn't running here, so they weren't compared. I don't expect changes, because the demo budget has no subcategories.
- **In the browser:** drag-and-drop, the delete dialog preselecting the parent, and the hidden template and "To Budget" options. Their logic is unit-tested, but I didn't see them on screen. The template option is behind a feature flag that's off in the test budget.

**One cosmetic issue:** the Σ marker sits near the top of the row, not vertically centred, and about 100px left of the amount it describes. I didn't fix it, since it's a design detail. It's probably a small style change if you want it.
